walkthroughs.body_html:
The Early Church: The Church in Acts — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Early Church: The Church in Acts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Early Church: The Church in Acts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the central principle of situation ethics?
options: You should do whatever feels right in the moment.
Situation ethics says rules should always be followed.
The only intrinsically good thing is agape love; rules can be broken if doing so produces the most loving outcome in the situation.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
The Torah is the same as the Book of Genesis.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
The first five books of the Hebrew Bible (Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy) — traditionally attributed to Moses and containing law, narrative and covenant.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Sunni and Shia Islam?
options: Sunnis and Shias believe in different gods.
Situation ethics says rules should always be followed.
They split over who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad: Sunnis accepted Abu Bakr and elected caliphs; Shias believed leadership should follow Muhammad's bloodline through Ali.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.
